questions.prompt: For \(x(t)=2t^3-t\), find \(v_x\), \(a_x\), and their values at \(t=1\,\mathrm{s}\).
If \(v_x(t)=4t\) and \(x(0)=3\,\mathrm{m}\), find \(x(t)\).
For \(x(t)=t^3-6t^2\), find when acceleration is zero.
For \(v_x(t)=3t^2-2\), find displacement from \(t=0\) to \(t=2\,\mathrm{s}\).
If \(v_x(t)=kt\) and \(x(0)=0\), find \(x(t)\).
For \(a_x(t)=2t+1\), find the velocity change from \(t=0\) to \(t=3\,\mathrm{s}\).
For \(x(t)=t^4\), find \(v_x(t)\) and \(a_x(t)\).
For \(x(t)=5+3t-2t^2\), find when the particle stops.
What physical quantity is represented by area under a velocity-time graph?
questions.answer:
The signed area gives displacement:
\[
\Delta x=\int_{t_i}^{t_f}v_x(t)\,dt
\]

questions.prompt: For \(x(t)=A\sin(\omega t)\), find \(v_x(t)\) and \(a_x(t)\).
For \(v_x(t)=6-2t\), find displacement from \(t=0\) to \(t=5\,\mathrm{s}\).
Check the units of \(\int v_x(t)\,dt\).
questions.answer:
Velocity has units \(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), and \(dt\) has units \(\mathrm{s}\):
\[
\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\cdot\mathrm{s}=\mathrm{m}
\]
So the integral has displacement units.

questions.prompt: If velocity is constant, what is acceleration?
Why are initial conditions needed after integration?
questions.answer: Integration introduces a constant. An initial condition fixes that constant, such as \(x(0)\) or \(v_x(0)\).

questions.prompt: For \(v_x(t)=t^2\), find displacement from \(t=1\,\mathrm{s}\) to \(t=3\,\mathrm{s}\).
Starting with \(a_y=-g\), integrate to get the free-fall velocity and position equations.
What physical quantity is represented by area under an acceleration-time graph?
questions.answer:
The signed area gives velocity change:
\[
\Delta v_x=\int_{t_i}^{t_f}a_x(t)\,dt
\]

questions.prompt: A particle has \(a_x(t)=6t-4\), \(v_x(0)=3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), and \(x(0)=-2\,\mathrm{m}\). Find \(v_x(t)\) and \(x(t)\).
A particle has \(v_x(t)=t^2-4t+3\). Find its displacement and distance traveled from \(t=0\) to \(t=4\,\mathrm{s}\).
questions.answer:
First find where velocity changes sign:
\[
t^2-4t+3=(t-1)(t-3)
\]
\[
\Delta x=\int_0^4(t^2-4t+3)\,dt=\left[\frac{t^3}{3}-2t^2+3t\right]_0^4=\frac{4}{3}\,\mathrm{m}
\]
For distance, split at \(t=1\) and \(t=3\), then add absolute displacements on each interval.
